title: Skin Layers Anatomy: Epidermal Strata, Dermis & Sensory
description: Study skin layers microanatomy from the five epidermal strata and basement membrane to papillary and reticular dermis, sweat glands, follicles, and nerves.
h1: Skin Layers and Appendages Microanatomy: Epidermal Strata and Dermis
blurb: Five epidermal keratinocyte strata, interlocking dermal papillae, reticular collagen bundles, eccrine and sebaceous glands, and specialized touch corpuscles.
lead: Zooming in on a few millimeters of human skin reveals a continuously renewing brick-and-mortar epithelium anchored to a vascular dermal web of collagen and nerve endings. In this illustrated guide to skin layers and epidermis anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including stratum basale, stratum spinosum, stratum granulosum, stratum lucidum—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Zooming in on a few millimeters of human skin reveals a continuously renewing brick-and-mortar epithelium anchored to a vascular dermal web of collagen and nerve endings. Epidermis is a stratified keratinizing epithelium nourished by diffusion from vascular dermis. From deep to superficial: basale, spinosum, granulosum, optional lucidum (most evident in thick skin), and corneum. Basement membrane joins epidermis to papillary dermis; reticular dermis provides strength. The hypodermis is adipose-rich subcutis beneath the dermis. Hair, sebaceous glands and most sweat glands are skin appendages; cutaneous receptors relay varied forms of mechanical and thermal input. Within the human body, the skin layers & appendages (Epidermis · dermis · tela subcutanea) is situated in whole-body integument; thick glabrous skin of palms/soles differs from thin hairy skin, receives arterial perfusion via dermal superficial and deep vascular plexuses; epidermis is avascular, and is innervated by cutaneous sensory afferents and sympathetic sudomotor/vasomotor fibers.

The stratum basale is deep single proliferative keratinocyte layer adjoining basement membrane. Physiologically, the stratum basale governs renews overlying epidermis. Structurally, the stratum spinosum comprises several layers of keratinocytes strongly joined by desmosomes. Physiologically, the stratum spinosum provides mechanical cohesion. Structurally, the stratum granulosum comprises flattened keratinocytes with keratohyalin granules and lipid-releasing lamellar bodies. Physiologically, the stratum granulosum governs builds the water-permeability barrier. The stratum lucidum is thin translucent transition zone most apparent in glabrous palms and soles. Physiologically, the stratum lucidum governs adds specialized layer in thick skin. Structurally, the stratum corneum comprises anucleate flattened corneocytes surrounded by intercellular lipid lamellae. Physiologically, the stratum corneum governs principal external permeability barrier. Structurally, the basement membrane zone (Junctio dermoepidermalis) comprises anchoring complex joining epidermis to dermis with hemidesmosomes and matrix. Physiologically, the basement membrane zone governs resists separation and supports renewal.

Clinically, regarding the stratum basale, basal-cell carcinoma derives from basal-type cells. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the stratum spinosum, desmosomal disruption causes epidermal blistering. In clinical pathology involving the stratum granulosum, barrier injury increases transepidermal water loss. Medical evaluation of the stratum lucidum also notes that do not expect a distinct lucidum in ordinary thin hairy skin.

questions.question: What are the five epidermal layers in thick skin?
questions.answer: From deep to superficial they are stratum basale, spinosum, granulosum, lucidum and corneum. Thin skin does not have a distinct lucidum.

questions.question: Does the epidermis have its own blood vessels?
questions.answer: No. The epidermis receives nutrients by diffusion from capillaries in the underlying dermis.

questions.question: What is the stratum basale?
questions.answer: The stratum basale is the deep, single-cell layer of proliferative keratinocytes adjoining the basement membrane.

questions.question: Where is the stratum granulosum located?
questions.answer: The stratum granulosum lies between the stratum spinosum and stratum corneum in the epidermis.

questions.question: What is the function of the stratum corneum?
questions.answer: The stratum corneum forms the epidermis’s outer permeability barrier and helps limit water loss.
